brief.title: Cooling the city: the case for street trees
brief.dek: A review for a city resilience committee compares heat exposure, tree cover, costs, and implementation time of urban cooling interventions.
brief.thesis: Mature street trees are a cost-effective, long-term urban cooling solution that also provides additional environmental and health benefits.

claims.text: Mature street trees cut peak street temperature by up to 4.2°C.
claims.label: peak street temperature reduction

claims.text: One mature tree can intercept about 1,400 litres of rainfall a year, reducing pressure on drains.
claims.label: rainfall interception

claims.text: Tree cover in the surveyed district fell from 29% to 21% over ten years.
claims.label: tree cover

claims.text: Residents in planted streets report fewer heat-illness days after two summers.
Maintenance costs for street trees are lower than installing and running new air conditioning.

relationships.summary: The committee's preferred program for street tree implementation runs in four stages.
items: water and maintain for two years
evaluate shade, rain interception, and resident health

relationships.summary: Different urban cooling interventions offer varying peak cooling, relative costs, and time to benefit.

brief.quote: The cheapest cooling is a tree that was planted ten years ago.
brief.bottom_line: Investing in a long-term street tree planting and maintenance program offers significant and sustainable urban cooling benefits, alongside other environmental and health advantages.
